ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The question states that ethanoic acid has a much lower vapor pressure than ethanol. Lower vapor pressure indicates that molecules escape into the gas phase less easily, so ethanoic acid must have stronger intermolecular attractions. Both ethanoic acid and ethanol have London dispersion forces and dipole-dipole interactions, and both contain an O-H group capable of hydrogen bonding. The key difference is that ethanoic acid has a carboxylic acid group, which can form especially strong hydrogen bonds between molecules. These stronger hydrogen-bonding attractions reduce vapor pressure.
